Experiments_conducted: BoDEx 2005 field experiment on surface winds, dust concentration and radiative effects; deflation and yardang studies (Bristow et al. 2009); MODIS dust tracking.
Experiments_that_can_be_conducted: Mars dust-lifting and saltation physics at the world's most active source: dust-devil and wind-gust lifting thresholds, dust-sensor and solar-panel cleaning tests, and electrostatic charging. Low-density diatomite (about 0.8 g/cm³) gives a direct test material for low-density Martian dust deposits. Yardangs in lake sediments are analogs for the Medusae Fossae Formation.
Parameter_similarity_summary: Composition/alteration 60; Water-ice/aridity 65; Sunlight/thermal latitude 85; Slope 95; Thermal inertia/dust 80; Roughness 60; Relief 30; Air density (elev.) 6; Temperature 10
Where_analogy_breaks: Very hot; security makes access difficult; diatomite is biogenic silica, not basaltic dust.
How_to_modify_artificially: Deploy Mars-like solar arrays and dust sensors; CO2 low-pressure wind tunnel on site using local diatomite; basaltic dust plots for comparison.
Justification: Fills GSOP's new dust column (dust_index in the thermal-inertia family). It emits the most dust of any place on Earth, has a dust-scale thermal-inertia surface and is flat. It has not been used as a Mars analog; the nearest Mars site in the list (Emi Koussi, also new) is about 330 km away.

Discovered_or_recognised: World Heritage 2016; MODIS hottest land-surface temperatures (Mildrexler et al. 2006)
First_used_as_analog: Minimal: remote-sensing comparisons (Foroutan & Zimbelman 2016 TAR analog; Aeolis yardang comparison 2025)
Experiments_conducted: Morphometric yardang studies (Ehsani & Quiel 2008; Mousavi 2015); TAR mega-ripple analog paper (Foroutan & Zimbelman 2016); comparison with Aeolis yardangs (2025); MODIS land-surface-temperature records.
Experiments_that_can_be_conducted: Field-validated yardang erosion rates to date Medusae Fossae and Aeolis terrain; TAR migration measurements; rover navigation through yardang corridors; extreme-heat thermal-cycling tests of hardware (day-night swing).
Parameter_similarity_summary: Composition/alteration 50; Water-ice/aridity 65; Sunlight/thermal latitude 85; Slope 80; Thermal inertia/dust 75; Roughness 80; Relief 55; Air density (elev.) 8; Temperature 10
Where_analogy_breaks: Extreme heat (Mars is cold); thick air; clays not basaltic.
How_to_modify_artificially: Night-time-only operations for thermal tests; basaltic simulant on corridor floors; wind-sensor networks.
Justification: One of Earth's largest mega-yardang and TAR fields, with high roughness and relief scores. Its use has been remote-sensing only, with no field operations, and it is more than 100 km from all known sites.

Process_type: Groundwater-fed inland sabkha (gypsum, halite, salt polygons)
Discovered_or_recognised: Known to Bedouin as 'Mother of Poisons'; crossed by Thesiger 1940s; geology by Fookes and others
Experiments_conducted: Sedimentology and hydrology only (deflation basin, Late Pleistocene lake-to-sabkha history); oil-exploration traverses.
Experiments_that_can_be_conducted: Analog for Martian chloride and sulfate deposits formed from upwelling groundwater (Meridiani, Terra Sirenum): mapping salt-polygon networks, testing groundwater-vs-runoff origin models, brine and biosignature sampling below the crust, and rover traction on deceptive crust over soft brine-mud (a mobility hazard analog like Spirit's embedding).
Parameter_similarity_summary: Composition/alteration 75; Water-ice/aridity 60; Sunlight/thermal latitude 85; Slope 98; Thermal inertia/dust 60; Roughness 35; Relief 15; Air density (elev.) 6; Temperature 15
GSOP_gate_check: Borderline - occasional flash floods and brine pools; passes in dry season
Where_analogy_breaks: Very hot; shallow liquid brine (Mars evaporites are ancient and dry); dunes and alluvial fans add quartz/carbonate.
How_to_modify_artificially: Instrumented crust plots with controlled evaporation; Mars-perchlorate spiking; drone-mapped polygon test grid for rover crust-breakthrough trials.
Justification: About 3,000 km² of almost perfectly flat, barren evaporite (top slope score), fed by groundwater. That process is central to the debate over how Martian chloride deposits formed. No Mars analog literature was found for it. It also has an engineering use as a hazardous-crust mobility test.
Scored_against: Jezero crater (minerals) + Arcadia Planitia (ground ice) - GSOP Mars v2 weights

Process_type: Hydrothermal carbonate-silica chimneys on a desiccating alkaline lake
Discovered_or_recognised: Chimneys described by early explorers; dated 2014 (Dekov et al.)
Experiments_conducted: Mineralogy and geochemistry of chimneys up to 60 m high, made of calcite and silica layers formed where hydrothermal fluids mix with lake water.
Experiments_that_can_be_conducted: Analog for Martian mounds and spring deposits and for lake carbonates (Jezero marginal carbonates): imaging-spectrometer mapping of carbonate-silica layering, biosignature preservation in chimneys, and rover/drone mapping of tall vertical structures. Also a site for lake-retreat shoreline mapping.
Parameter_similarity_summary: Composition/alteration 75; Water-ice/aridity 40; Sunlight/thermal latitude 76; Slope 90; Thermal inertia/dust 60; Roughness 65; Relief 40; Air density (elev.) 7; Temperature 5
GSOP_gate_check: Borderline - remaining lake covers part of tile
Where_analogy_breaks: Very hot; active springs and a living lake (with flamingos); thick air.
How_to_modify_artificially: Work on dry chimney fields away from the shore; cover active vents for clean sampling.
Justification: Rare on-land hydrothermal carbonate-silica chimneys in a desert, which raises its composition score. It has no analog use, and Dallol, the nearest known site, is about 380 km away.

Process_type: Sandstone plateau dissected by dendritic valleys; hyper-arid
First_used_as_analog: Minimal: Viking-era comparisons of Western Desert aeolian features (El-Baz et al. 1979)
Experiments_conducted: Desert geomorphology and Shuttle-radar discovery of buried palaeo-drainages in the Western Desert; prehistoric rock-art surveys; Viking-era aeolian comparisons.
Experiments_that_can_be_conducted: Analog for Martian valley networks cut into plateaux: drone-mapped dendritic wadis vs Warrego Valles, testing groundwater sapping vs runoff, and radar sounding of buried channels (like SHARAD/RIMFAX).
Parameter_similarity_summary: Composition/alteration 40; Water-ice/aridity 70; Sunlight/thermal latitude 85; Slope 55; Thermal inertia/dust 70; Roughness 65; Relief 75; Air density (elev.) 14; Temperature 15
Where_analogy_breaks: Sandstone not basalt; very hot; remote.
How_to_modify_artificially: Basaltic simulant aprons; GPR test lines; drone LiDAR baselines.
Justification: Dendritic valleys in one of the driest places on Earth, with strong relief and water-aridity scores. There has been no modern analog campaign. It is about 150 km from Kamil crater.
